title: Hissy Words Add ES
kidRule: Most words just add S to mean more than one. But when a word ends in a hissing or buzzing sound (S, X, Z, CH or SH), add ES so you can hear the extra beat: peach becomes peaches.
hint: Clap the word. Can you hear an extra beat at the end, after the hissing sound? One letter on its own cannot make that beat.
reminder: After S, X, Z, C-H or S-H, add E-S to mean more than one.

check.question: Why does PEACHES end in ES instead of just S?
check.correctAnswer: PEACH ends in C-H, a hissing sound, so we add ES to make an extra beat we can say!
distractors: Because all words about food add ES
Because the E is there to make the A say its name

words.why: PEACH ends in C-H, so it adds E-S to mean more than one.
words.def: Soft, round, fuzzy fruits with a big stone inside.
words.sent: We picked ripe peaches from the tree.
words.story: A nectarine is really a kind of peach with smooth skin instead of fuzzy skin!
words.card: *Each* monkey got two *peaches* and a tiny hat!

words.card: The giraffe wore *glasses* made from two *glass* jars!

words.card: The crab made *sandwiches* out of *sand* and seaweed!
